questions.question_text:
A town produces $6$ tonnes of rubbish this year, and the amount increases by $25\%$ each year.
Which model gives the rubbish $W$ tonnes after $n$ years?

options.why: Subtracted the rate instead of adding it, which models a $25\%$ decrease.
Swapped the initial value and the rate, using $25$ as the initial amount.
Wrote $25\%$ as $0.025$ instead of $0.25$.

questions.solution_text:
The initial value is $k=6$.
An increase of $25\%$ gives $a=1+0.25=1.25$.
$W=6(1.25)^{n}$

questions.question_text:
A scooter is worth $\$900$ and loses $40\%$ of its value each year.
Which model gives its value $V$ dollars after $n$ years?

options.why: Added the rate instead of subtracting it, which models a $40\%$ increase.
Used the rate itself as the base instead of $1-0.4$.
Wrote $40\%$ as $0.04$ instead of $0.40$.

questions.solution_text:
The initial value is $k=900$.
A decrease of $40\%$ gives $a=1-0.4=0.6$.
$V=900(0.6)^{n}$

questions.question_text:
A quantity is modelled by $A=150(1.6)^{x}$.
Find $A$ when $x=4$.

options.why: Multiplied $150$ by the base and then by $4$, instead of raising the base to the power $4$.
Used a power of $3$ instead of $4$, one period too few.
Used a power of $5$ instead of $4$, one period too many.

questions.question_text:
A quantity is modelled by $y=972(3)^{-x}$.
Find $y$ when $x=4$.

options.why: Divided by $3^{3}$ instead of $3^{4}$, one period too few.
Divided by $3^{5}$ instead of $3^{4}$, one period too many.
Treated the negative index as making the answer negative rather than as a reciprocal.

questions.question_text:
The table shows an exponential relationship.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline y & 7 & 28 & 112 & 448 \end{array}$
Which equation fits the table?

options.why: Used the first difference $28-7=21$ as the base instead of the ratio $28\div 7$.
Took the value at $x=1$ as the initial value instead of the value at $x=0$.
Took the value at $x=1$ as the initial value and used the first difference $28-7=21$ as the base.

questions.question_text: For the model $y=2(3)^{x}$, what is the smallest whole number value of $x$ for which $y$ is greater than $500$?

options.why: Chose the last value still below $500$ rather than the first value above it.
Continued one row past the first value that exceeds $500$.
Divided $500$ by $2$ instead of testing values of $x$ in the model.

questions.solution_text:
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} x & 5 & 6 & 7 \\ \hline y & 486 & 1458 & 4374 \end{array}$
At $x=5$, $y=486$, which is below $500$.
At $x=6$, $y=1458$, which is above $500$.
The smallest whole number value is $x=6$.

questions.question_text:
A sample of a substance has a mass of $250$ g, and after one hour its mass is $200$ g. The decay is exponential.
Which model gives the mass $m$ grams after $t$ hours?

options.why: Divided the masses the wrong way round as $\frac{250}{200}=1.25$, giving a growth base for a decaying sample.
Used the mass after one hour as the initial value instead of the mass at $t=0$.
Used the mass after one hour as the initial value and divided the masses the wrong way round as $\frac{250}{200}=1.25$.
Treated the jump from $x=0$ to $x=2$ as a single step, so $\frac{108}{12}=9$ was used as the base.
Read the height at $x=1$ as the initial value instead of the height where the curve meets the vertical axis.
Read the height at $x=1$ as the initial value and treated $x=0$ to $x=2$ as a single step, giving the base $\frac{108}{12}=9$.

questions.solution_text:
The curve meets the vertical axis at $y=12$, so $k=12$.
At $x=1$ the curve is at $y=36$, so $a=\frac{36}{12}=3$.
$y=12(3)^{x}$

questions.question_text: How many pieces of information are needed in order to fix the parameters in an exponential model?

options.why: One condition generally fixes only one relation, not both model parameters.
Adds an unnecessary condition when the two model parameters are independent.
Uses more information than is needed to determine two parameters.

questions.solution_text: A basic exponential model has two independent parameters, for example $y=ab^x$. Two independent pieces of information are therefore needed to determine $a$ and $b$.

questions.question_text:
Eric is investigating the growth in the population of a type of bacteria.
At the start of day 1, there are 1000 bacteria in Eric’s flask.
The population of bacteria grows exponentially at the rate of 60% per day.
How many bacteria are in the flask at the end of the 4th day?

options.why: Applies the daily growth only once.
Uses an incorrect linear or partial growth calculation.
Applies only three daily growth factors instead of four.

questions.solution_text: A $60%$ daily increase multiplies the population by $1.6$. After four days the population is $1000(1.6)^4=6553.6$.
